questions.question: What must be in a vehicle when transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine must carry an approved gas mask in the vehicle. They must also have an emergency kit to control leaks in the cargo tank's dome cover plate fittings.

questions.question: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Either awake or asleep inside the vehicle.

questions.explanation: A person attending a parked placarded vehicle must either be awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. If outside the vehicle, they must have a clear view of it. They cannot be in the sleeper berth.

questions.question: What should you do before opening trailer doors during a truck fire?

options.text: Check if the doors are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if the doors are hot.
questions.explanation: During a truck fire, always feel the doors first to check if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. If the doors are hot, keep them closed.

questions.question: Explosive materials are classified as what hazard class?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are items that can explode or catch fire.

questions.question: Who is responsible for identifying the hazard class of materials being shipped?
questions.explanation: The shipper must identify the product's identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class, packing group, and ensure correct packaging, labels, marking, and placards.

questions.question: Which agency conducts the background check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts the background check required to get a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: How should you label a hazardous material item if the label is too large for the package?

options.text: Tie the item with other hazardous materials and attach a labeled paper to the outside.
Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
Mark the item with a large orange dot.
Place the item in a box with a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
questions.explanation: Shippers must use diamond-shaped hazard warning labels on hazardous materials packages. If the label does not fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: How should identification numbers, shipping names, and hazard classes appear on shipping papers?

options.text: They may be abbreviated if space is limited.
They should be abbreviated to make them easier to read.
They may be abbreviated if easy to understand.

questions.explanation: Identification numbers, shipping names, and hazard classes must always be written in full on shipping papers. The only exception is if the abbreviation is specifically allowed by hazardous materials regulations.

questions.question: When can an improperly placarded vehicle be driven?

options.text: If it does not contain radioactive materials

questions.explanation: A vehicle carrying hazardous materials must be properly placarded to drive. An improperly placarded vehicle may only be driven if necessary to protect life or property in an emergency.

questions.question: How should you label a package if the hazardous materials label does not fit on it?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the item.
Attach a QR code to be scanned.
Reduce the label size to fit it on the item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the item.
questions.explanation: Shippers must place diamond-shaped hazard warning labels on hazardous materials packages. If the label will not fit on the package, place it on a tag that is securely attached to the package instead.

questions.question: What does a driver need to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
A CDL with a tank endorsement
A CDL with a cargo endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: On a shipping paper, should the identification number, shipping name, and hazard class be abbreviated?

options.text: Yes, if using a small piece of paper.
Yes, if the abbreviations are easy to understand.

questions.explanation: On hazardous materials shipping papers, the identification number, shipping name, and hazard class must never be abbreviated unless the hazardous materials regulations specifically allow it.

questions.question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher rating required on a placarded vehicle?
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: When loading a tank with flammable liquids, what should you do?

options.text: Establish a ground before opening the filling hole.
Break a ground right before opening the filling hole.
Lock the filling hole during loading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Establish a ground before opening the filling hole.
questions.explanation: Before loading or unloading a tank with flammable liquids, turn off the engine unless needed to run a pump. Ground the tank before opening the filling hole and keep it grounded until after closing the hole.

questions.question: Which is NOT your job as a driver at an accident scene with hazardous materials?

options.text: Keeping people away from the scene.
Trying to put out a hazardous materials fire.
Telling emergency responders about the hazardous materials danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trying to put out a hazardous materials fire.
questions.explanation: Your job is to keep people away, tell emergency responders about the hazards, and provide shipping papers. Do not try to fight hazardous materials fires unless you have protective equipment and training.

questions.question: Who can transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A driver with a CDL and hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to operate any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: How must containers of hazardous materials be secured?

options.text: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.
Limited to a maximum of four feet tall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.
questions.explanation: Containers of hazardous materials must be braced so they do not fall, slide, or bounce during transportation.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: How far away must a person be to smoke near a vehicle placarded for Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials?
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle placarded for Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases). Never smoke near vehicles carrying flammable or explosive materials.

questions.question: Who is responsible for labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials. The shipper must also supply the warning placards.

questions.question: Your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery. After delivery, turn off the engine ____ unhooking the hoses.
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine after the product transfer but before unhooking the hoses.

questions.question: Containers of hazardous materials must be:

options.text: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.
questions.explanation: Brace containers so they will not fall, slide, or bounce around during transportation. All hazardous materials packages must be secured.

questions.question: Chemical identification numbers can be found in:
questions.explanation: The DOT Emergency Response Guide (ERG) contains information about hazardous chemicals. It is indexed by the proper shipping names and identification numbers of substances.

questions.question: A manifest for transporting hazardous waste:

options.text: Must be attached to the outside of the trailer.

questions.explanation: If you transport hazardous waste, you must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. The manifest must be signed by hand.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, the trailer should be:

options.text: Left to air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Parts of a vehicle exposed to corrosive liquids must be thoroughly washed with water.

questions.question: The correct way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tire with your hand.
Measuring the height of the tire.

questions.explanation: Check your tires at the start of every trip and after every stop. Use a tire pressure gauge to check that tires are properly inflated.

questions.question: A shipping paper:

options.text: Is not needed for most shipments of hazardous materials.
Is required for all shipments of hazardous materials.
Can be kept in a digital file.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required for all shipments of hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Shippers must provide proper shipping papers for all hazardous materials shipments. These papers communicate the risks of the materials.

questions.question: If required, ____ identical placards must be placed on a vehicle.
questions.explanation: When placards are required, display four identical placards on a vehicle. Place one on the front, rear, and both sides.

questions.question: If transporting chlorine, what must be in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine in cargo tanks, you must have an approved gas mask in your vehicle.

questions.question: Who must label hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials. They must also supply any necessary placards.
